messages:
alex: heads-up — got a support ticket from NimbusPay: users seeing 429s + tail latency spikes on their Dedicated pool starting ~03:15 UTC. Scale kept bouncing 4->1->4 over ~20m.
maya: ugh. any error patterns in the API gateway?
alex: gateway shows bursts of queued requests then a lot of `rate_limited` responses. attached logs show repeated connect retries from same tenant-id.
maya: can you drop the grafana links? curious about the autoscaler decision timeline.
alex: https://grafana.internal/r/nbp/tenant-nimbuspay/autoscale?from=1700000000&to=1700002000 
alex: key panels: `active_rps`, `latency_p95`, `pool_instances`. you'll see sawtooth.
sre-oncall: adding context — our autoscaler policy for Dedicated uses an `rps` target with cooldown 120s, but also a burst detector that can trigger short-lived scale-ups for sustained >2x baseline.
tom: pinging platform-bot for metric dump. @platform-bot can you snapshot the last 40m for tenant=nimbuspay?
platform-bot: snapshot complete: /artifacts/nbp-1799991234/metrics.tar.gz : includes `instance_cpu`, `kv_cache_hit`, `req_sequence_len_distribution`, `rps`.
maya: quick hypothesis: KV cache thrash from a tenant-side pattern (large prefixed prompts) causing per-request latency to spike -> autoscaler sees high rps/latency -> scales up -> after scale new instances cold miss cache -> latency stays high -> autoscaler scales back down on metric noise. pendulum effect.
alex: that matches logs — many requests include long prompt prefixes. also saw `kv_cache_eviction` logs at the same times.
sre-oncall: repro attempt suggestion: we should simulate tenant workload with sequence length distribution matching their traffic (heavy prefix reuse but high cardinality). I can run load test on staging pool with `redwoodctl loadtest`.
tom: runbook notes — try changing autoscaler to use `stable_rps` (median over 60s) instead of raw `rps` for scale decisions, and increase cooldown to 240s before we flip flags. Also consider `warmup_cache=true` for new instances to prefetch popular prefixes.
maya: low-risk mitigation: set per-tenant burst throttle at routing layer to smooth the incoming burst (rate-limit short spikes but keep overall SLA).
alex: contacting NimbusPay support lead to request example prompts + approximate client concurrency. also told them we may do a config change and will notify before rolling.
sre-oncall: I'll open an incident ticket and schedule a canary deploy of cooldown=240s on a single AZ for 15m. if pendulum stops, we roll further. if not, we escalate to runtime team for deeper cache sharding.
platform-bot: incident created: INC-2026-394 (link: https://incidents.internal/INC-2026-394). assigned: maya, sre-oncall.
tom: commands I used to inspect tenant pool:```bash
redwoodctl pools list --tenant=nimbuspay
redwoodctl metrics query --pool nbp-prod --range 40m --expr "autoscale_decision_events"
kubectl logs svc/dedicated-nbp --since=30m | grep kv_cache_eviction
```
maya: after canary, I'll capture `prefetch` traces and KV cache hit rates. if warmup reduces miss rate <10% we can keep warmup flag.
alex: thanks all — I'll keep NimbusPay updated. will post follow-ups in this thread with results + timeline. :thumbsup:
